more_info.overview: Aspartame-acesulfame salt combines the two sweetener components in a crystalline material produced under acidic conditions. Its stabilising role is to help a food maintain its physical consistency or the distribution of its ingredients. Made by combining aspartame and acesulfame potassium in acidic solution and crystallising the resulting salt. Potassium and moisture are removed during processing. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit nectars as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable nectars and similar products; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Made by combining aspartame and acesulfame potassium in acidic solution and crystallising the resulting salt. Potassium and moisture are removed during processing.
more_info.daily_intake: Component limits: 40 mg aspartame/kg body weight/day and 15 mg acesulfame K/kg body weight/day (EFSA, 2026). No separate salt ADI was derived.
more_info.side_effects:
The salt separates into its two sweetener components. Their assessed food-use exposure raised no concern in 2026.
The assessment applies the separate component intake limits.
